title: Introducing the Model Context Protocol
summary: Anthropic open-sourced the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting AI assistants to data sources such as content repositories, business tools and development environments. The launch included the specification and SDKs on GitHub, local MCP server support in Claude Desktop, and pre-built servers for Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, Git, Postgres and Puppeteer. Anthropic named Block and Apollo as early integrators and said Zed, Replit, Codeium and Sourcegraph were working with MCP.
relevance: This is the origin event for the agent-to-tool layer that later handoff and migration designs assume as a common substrate.
search_query: Anthropic introducing the Model Context Protocol November 2024
notes: No individual author listed on page; MCP creators named elsewhere as David Soria Parra and Justin Spahr-Summers.

title: OpenAI adopts rival Anthropic's standard for connecting AI models to data
summary: TechCrunch reported that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced on X that OpenAI would support MCP across its products. Support was available immediately in the OpenAI Agents SDK, with the ChatGPT desktop app and the Responses API to follow. Anthropic CPO Mike Krieger welcomed the move, and the article notes Block, Apollo, Replit, Codeium and Sourcegraph had already adopted MCP.
relevance: Cross-vendor adoption by Anthropic's main competitor made MCP tool definitions portable across agent frameworks, a precondition for moving agents between stacks without rewriting tool integrations.
search_query: OpenAI adopts Anthropic Model Context Protocol TechCrunch
notes: Primary source is Altman's X post (not fetched); TechCrunch used as the dated record.

title: MCP Security Notification: Tool Poisoning Attacks
summary: Invariant Labs disclosed Tool Poisoning Attacks, in which malicious instructions hidden in MCP tool descriptions are seen by the model but not the user. In a Cursor experiment, a poisoned 'add' tool made the agent read ~/.cursor/mcp.json and SSH keys and pass them to the attacker's server. The post also described 'rug pulls' (a server changing tool descriptions after approval) and 'tool shadowing' (one server's description hijacking a trusted send_email tool), and recommended tool pinning and cross-server dataflow controls.
relevance: Shows that tool metadata travelling with an agent is an attack surface, so any portable task context or handoff must treat tool descriptions as untrusted and integrity-pinned.
search_query: Invariant Labs tool poisoning attacks MCP security notification

title: Securing the Model Context Protocol: Building a safer agentic future on Windows
summary: At Build 2025, Microsoft said Windows 11 would adopt MCP as a foundation for agentic computing, announcing an early private developer preview. Microsoft says all MCP client-server traffic will go through a trusted Windows proxy for policy, consent, authentication and auditing, and that only servers meeting baseline criteria (code signing, immutable tool definitions, declared privileges) will appear in a central Windows MCP registry. It also described per-tool user authorization and runtime isolation, with some controls not enforced during the preview.
relevance: An OS-level mediating proxy and registry is a concrete model for where policy, consent and audit sit when agent tool access moves between machines and hosts.
search_query: Windows 11 Model Context Protocol Build 2025 agentic OS blog securing MCP

title: Asana's cutting-edge AI feature ran into a little data leakage problem
summary: The Register reported that a bug in Asana's MCP server, launched as an experimental beta on 1 May 2025, could have exposed one organization's data to other Asana MCP users. Asana found the flaw on 4 June 2025, took the feature offline from 5 to 17 June, and reset all MCP connections. Asana did not say how many customers were affected, and there was no indication of exploitation.
relevance: A cross-tenant leak in a hosted MCP server illustrates why tenant isolation and scoped identity must survive when agents reach shared remote tool endpoints.
search_query: Asana MCP server bug data exposure customers 2025
notes: Other outlets cite about 1,000 affected customers; The Register says Asana did not disclose a number.

title: Critical RCE Vulnerability in Anthropic MCP Inspector - CVE-2025-49596
summary: Oligo Security described CVE-2025-49596 (CVSS 9.4), a remote code execution flaw in Anthropic's MCP Inspector developer tool affecting versions below 0.14.1. Because the Inspector client and proxy did not authenticate each other, JavaScript on a malicious web page could send a cross-site request to the proxy on 0.0.0.0:6277 and launch arbitrary stdio commands; a DNS rebinding variant was also shown. Anthropic's fix added a default session token and origin verification.
relevance: Unauthenticated local proxies are a recurring weak point in MCP tooling, relevant to any design that relocates agents onto developer machines or shared hosts.
search_query: Oligo Security MCP Inspector critical RCE vulnerability CVE-2025-49596 blog
notes: GitHub advisory published 2025-06-13; Oligo blog dated 2025-06-27.

title: Critical RCE Vulnerability in mcp-remote: CVE-2025-6514 Threatens LLM Clients
summary: JFrog Security Research disclosed CVE-2025-6514 (CVSS 9.6) in mcp-remote, a proxy that lets local MCP clients connect to remote servers, affecting versions 0.0.5 to 0.1.15 and fixed in 0.1.16. A malicious or hijacked server could return a crafted OAuth authorization_endpoint that mcp-remote passed to the OS browser launcher, giving full command execution on Windows and limited executable launch on macOS and Linux. JFrog says this was the first full client-side RCE in a real-world MCP scenario.
relevance: The OAuth discovery step is where an agent crosses trust boundaries to a new server, and this flaw shows that metadata from the remote side must be validated before any action.
search_query: JFrog mcp-remote CVE-2025-6514 remote code execution

title: Introducing the MCP Registry
summary: The MCP maintainers launched the official MCP Registry in preview at registry.modelcontextprotocol.io as an open catalog and API for publicly available MCP servers. The registry and its OpenAPI specification are open source so that public marketplaces and private enterprise sub-registries can build on it, and maintainers can denylist servers reported for spam, malicious code or impersonation. The preview carries no durability guarantees and may introduce breaking changes before general availability.
relevance: A canonical discovery and identity record for servers lets a relocated or delegated agent re-resolve the same tools in a new environment.
search_query: "Introducing the MCP Registry" modelcontextprotocol blog September 2025

title: One line of malicious npm code led to massive Postmark email heist
summary: The Register reported Koi Security's discovery of 'postmark-mcp', an npm package that impersonated Postmark's MCP server. After 15 clean versions, version 1.0.16 added one line that blind-copied every outgoing email to an attacker-controlled address. Koi says the package had about 1,500 weekly downloads and estimates about 300 organizations used it actively; Postmark said it had no connection to the package and its systems were not breached.
relevance: The first widely reported in-the-wild malicious MCP server shows that supply-chain provenance has to be part of any portable tool manifest.
search_query: postmark-mcp malicious MCP server npm Koi Security The Register
notes: Primary disclosure is Koi Security's blog (not fetched); exposure figures are Koi's estimates.

title: One Year of MCP: November 2025 Spec Release
summary: On MCP's first anniversary the maintainers released specification version 2025-11-25. It added experimental Tasks (SEP-1686), so any request can be wrapped in a pollable task with working, input-required, completed, failed and cancelled states, and allowed client registration via OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents (SEP-991). It also added machine-to-machine client credentials (SEP-1046), enterprise IdP controls (SEP-990), URL-mode elicitation (SEP-1036), sampling with tools (SEP-1577) and an extensions framework.
relevance: Pollable tasks with explicit states are a direct building block for checkpoint/resume and handoff of long-running agent work.
search_query: "One Year of MCP" November 2025 spec release blog

title: Donating the Model Context Protocol and establishing the Agentic AI Foundation
summary: Anthropic announced it is donating MCP to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), a directed fund under the Linux Foundation co-founded by Anthropic, Block and OpenAI with support from Google, Microsoft, AWS, Cloudflare and Bloomberg. Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md joined as founding projects. Anthropic said there were more than 10,000 active public MCP servers and over 97 million monthly SDK downloads, and that MCP's governance model would stay unchanged.
relevance: Vendor-neutral governance makes MCP a credible long-term interoperability layer for moving agent work across organizations.
search_query: Anthropic donates Model Context Protocol Agentic AI Foundation Linux Foundation

title: Google Cloud Launches Managed MCP Support
summary: InfoQ reported that Google Cloud announced fully managed remote MCP servers in public preview, giving agents and MCP clients such as Gemini CLI a single enterprise endpoint for Google services. Rollout starts with Google Maps, BigQuery, Compute Engine and GKE, with tools discoverable through a Cloud API Registry and Apigee API Hub. Apigee can also turn existing enterprise APIs into MCP servers under existing governance.
relevance: Managed remote MCP endpoints from a hyperscaler move tool access off the agent's host, which makes agents easier to relocate without carrying local servers along.
search_query: Google announces fully managed remote MCP servers Google Cloud services
notes: Google's own announcement (around 10 Dec 2025 per The New Stack) was not fetched; InfoQ used as the dated record.

title: MCP Apps - Bringing UI Capabilities To MCP Clients
summary: The MCP maintainers announced MCP Apps as the first official MCP extension, letting tools return interactive UI components rendered in a sandboxed iframe that talks to the host over JSON-RPC via postMessage. Supporting clients named were Claude (web and desktop), Goose, VS Code Insiders and ChatGPT. The extension builds on the November 2025 proposal derived from MCP-UI and the OpenAI Apps SDK, and hosts can require user consent for UI-initiated tool calls.
relevance: Standardised tool UIs let the same server-delivered interface follow an agent task across different host applications.
search_query: MCP Apps extension announcement OpenAI Anthropic MCP-UI blog

title: The 2026 MCP Roadmap
summary: The MCP lead maintainer reorganised the roadmap around four priority areas run by Working Groups rather than release dates: transport scalability (stateless, horizontally scalable Streamable HTTP and .well-known capability metadata), agent communication (retry and expiry semantics for SEP-1686 Tasks), governance maturation (delegating SEP acceptance to trusted Working Groups) and enterprise readiness (audit trails, SSO-integrated auth, gateways, configuration portability). The post said no new official transports would be added this cycle and noted SEP-1932 (DPoP) and SEP-1933 (Workload Identity Federation) were in review.
relevance: Stateless transport, task lifecycle and configuration portability are the protocol changes that most directly determine whether agent work can relocate between hosts.

title: The Mother of All AI Supply Chains: Critical, Systemic Vulnerability at the Core of Anthropic's MCP
summary: OX Security says the stdio transport in the official MCP SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Java, Rust) lets any input that reaches a server's launch configuration run as an OS command. OX claims the issue affects 150M+ downloads and up to 200,000 instances, reports 30+ disclosures and 10+ High/Critical CVEs in downstream projects (e.g. LiteLLM, Windsurf, DocsGPT), and says 9 of 11 MCP registries accepted poisoned entries in testing. According to OX, Anthropic called the behaviour expected and declined an architectural change, leaving input sanitisation to developers.
relevance: Server launch configuration is part of what moves when an agent's tool set is copied to a new host, so this finding bears directly on safe relocation and migration.
search_query: OX Security MCP STDIO "by design" vulnerability Anthropic SDK April 2026
notes: Scale figures and Anthropic's response are as reported by OX; Anthropic's own statement was not fetched. The OX CVE table lists CVE-2026-33224 twice (Bisheng and Jaaz), possibly a page error.

title: The AWS MCP Server is now generally available
summary: AWS announced general availability of the AWS MCP Server, a managed remote MCP server that is part of the Agent Toolkit for AWS and gives coding agents authenticated access to AWS services. AWS says it adds a single tool able to call any AWS API including long-running operations, sandboxed Python execution, and on-demand agent skills since the re:Invent 2025 preview. Governance relies on IAM guardrails, CloudWatch metrics and CloudTrail logging; it is offered at no extra charge in US East (N. Virginia) and Europe (Frankfurt).
relevance: Ties MCP tool calls to cloud IAM identity and audit logs, which is the accountability chain that has to persist when agent work moves between runtimes.

title: The 2026-07-28 Specification
summary: The maintainers released MCP specification 2026-07-28, removing the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header so each request carries its version, client identity and capabilities in _meta. Server-initiated requests now use multi round-trip results (SEP-2322), Streamable HTTP requests must carry Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name routing headers (SEP-2243), and list results get cache hints (SEP-2549). Authorization was hardened (issuer validation per RFC 9207, issuer-bound credentials, deprecation of Dynamic Client Registration in favour of CIMD), Tasks moved to an extension (SEP-2663), and Roots, Sampling, Logging and legacy HTTP+SSE were deprecated with at least a twelve-month window.
relevance: A stateless core means no session needs to be migrated, so an MCP client or server can be relocated or load-balanced between requests, which simplifies runtime relocation.
notes: Anthropic's companion post 'Bringing MCP 2026-07-28 to Claude' (same date) claims 400M+ monthly SDK downloads; not included as a separate item to avoid duplicating the event.

title: The New MCP Roadmap
summary: After the 2026-07-28 release the maintainers published a new roadmap with five priority areas: agentic messaging primitives (server-initiated events, moving the Tasks extension SEP-2663 into the core spec), consolidation on Streamable HTTP including for local servers that now use stdio, agent identity and enterprise security, improved primitives (a single tools/call result contract and progressive tool discovery), and SDK developer experience. The identity work covers finalising DPoP and defining an agent identity and delegation path using Workload Identity Federation, the ID-JAG grant and standard token exchange, with engagement in the IETF OAuth and WIMSE groups.
relevance: An explicit agent identity and delegation path built on token exchange is the accountability mechanism that delegation and handoff research needs at the tool layer.
